newsitem.title: UK: Insurance market expects US merger for Sedgwick.
newsitem.headline: Insurance market expects US merger for Sedgwick.

text.p: Expectations in the UK insurance market are growing that London-based broker Sedgwick Group Plc will merge with a U.S. rival, but the company is sticking to its no comment line.

Many market watchers are convinced that Sedgwick will merge with New York-based Marsh & McLennan in a move which would secure the U.S. company as the world's largest broker -- a position challenged last week by the takeover of Alexander & Alexander by giant U.S. rival Aon.
Even members of staff in some Sedgwick departments believe an announcement is imminent.
But Sedgwick spokeswoman Julia Fish said she was unable to comment other than to say: "Our share price remains pretty static, and as far as we are concerned it's just another normal day."

Sedgwick heightened the speculation stakes itself in August when chief executive Sax Riley suggested a merger with another broker was possible, adding that there was room for only three or four big players in the global insurance broking market.

The Aon /A&A deal has reduced the number to five, while Monday's smaller deal between Lloyd Thompson and JIB Group demonstrates that the pressures are still there for brokers to consolidate and reduce costs.
Against this background, the options open to Sedgwick are either a merger with one of the other big four brokers or the acquisition of one or more smaller brokers.
Riley has played down a merger with UK rival Willis Corroon Group Plc. Market sources say talks have taken place between the two, but have so far led nowhere.
Apart from Aon, which is busy digesting A&A, that leaves only Marsh & McLennan and privately owned J&H as possible merger partners.
Acquiring smaller brokers is fraught with problems, as many have suffered severely in recent years and would not necessarily add much in terms of global reach.
With Sedgwick's share price little moved at 133-1/2, up 1-1/2 pemce, the stockmarket does not share the sentiment within the insurance broking sector itself that an announcement is imminent.
However, as long as the drivers for Sedgwick and other brokers to reduce costs remain, talk of acquisitions and mergers is likely to continue unabated.
